references.text: Abraham offers to fetch water to wash the guests' feet, a direct parallel image of hospitality and service that Jesus performs.
Lot also offers to wash his guests' feet, showing that this was a common but especially humble act of service in the ancient world.
Eliezer is given water to wash the feet and camels, an action that underscores the role of hospitality in preparing for an important meeting.
Jesus reminds us that he never received water to wash his feet, which contrasts with his own action in John 13 and emphasizes humility.
Paul mentions washing the saints' feet as an example of good works and service expected of Christian leaders.
